newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's privatization bond bill goes to Congress.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's privatization bond bill goes to Congress.

text.p: A bill allowing Brazilians to use credits with a workers fund to buy shares in the country's privatization program has been sent to Congress for approval, a presidential spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman said the bill was sent to Congress late Monday.

A Planning Ministry spokeswoman said the bill would allow workers to deposit up to 50 percent of their credits with the Time Served Guarantee Fund (FGTS) into privately managed mutual funds dedicated to privatized companies.
Employers in Brazil currently pay an equivalent of eight percent of their employees' salaries into the FGTS which the workers may claim once they leave their job.
The government has said it intends to earmark for bonds about six billion reais it owes to the FGTS fund in the hope of widening the base of investors taking part in Brazil's privatization program.
The government also hopes the funds would be up and running in time for next year's global offering of shares in mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, part of the company's privatization.
